analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/provider-process-exit-wait.md, lines 1-3) and a small addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, new prose at head lines 2964-2966). No executable source, configuration, key handling, attestation, WebSocket, prefix-cache or encryption code changed. The prose describes the cluster restart line reading FileVault via `fdesetup isactive` with a 5 s timeout, then SIGTERM, then 2 s more, and unknown on no answer. The changelog describes `ProcessExitObserver` reporting child exit sooner and no longer running the calling thread's run loop for launchctl, codesign, profiles, open and log. It states that timeouts and SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL escalation are unchanged. I found no documentation-level regression against the threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, T-041 and related). The docs make no claim that weakens an existing mitigation, and add no endpoint, secret or trust-boundary change. Open question for integration: the actual ProcessExitObserver implementation and its callers are not in the supplied evidence. I did not verify whether the timeout and SIGKILL escalation really remain intact, or whether a race between exit detection and pipe draining could drop output from codesign, signature-check or attestation-related probes and so change a trust decision. Those are unverified implementation contracts, not findings. The next pass should review the Swift code if it is in another batch. This is not a full audit.
